newsitem.title: LATVIA: C.BANKS MARKS 5TH ANNIVERSARY OF MONEY REFORM.
newsitem.headline: C.BANKS MARKS 5TH ANNIVERSARY OF MONEY REFORM.

text.p: The central bank on Wednesday celebrated the fifth anniversary of Latvia's departure from the post-Soviet rouble zone, saying the introduction of new currencies helped inflation and avoided a payments crisis.
Latvia in 1992 made its first step from the rouble zone by introducing a Latvian rouble at the rate of one lat to one rouble and in July that year it became the only currency.
In early 1993, it began to issue the new national currency the lat which is pegged at 0.7997 to the SDR.

"From early on in the reform we followed a liberal policy and no other currencies were banned from circulation according to the free market rate," central bank chief Einar Repshe told a news conference.
"The reform allowed us radically to reduce inflation to 35 percent in 1993 from 960 percent in 1992, which was a tenfold reduction," he added.
He noted that inflation this year is expected to stay below 10 percent in 1997 against last year's 13 percent.
